verification_report.summary:
The full supplied proof is correct under the stated accepted inputs. All deductions were checked sequentially in 14 statement-check records, with four reference checks. This includes the expressly accepted bounded noncollapsing and domination inputs being audited separately in singular_domination_01; this run verifies their applications, not that separate reconstruction.

The subsolution lemma works for a genuine qpsh rho without analytic singularities. Holder requires only the finite moment of order 2nqp/(p-q). For the auxiliary density 1+(-rho)^(2n)f, the fixed Hermitian Gauduchon estimate bounds the scalar above, the accepted lower density-norm estimate bounds it away from zero, and the potential estimate bounds v. The transform chi(t)=-1/t-1 has the correct range and derivative signs. Semipositivity makes h_k=max(rho+av,-k) admissible and makes every chain-rule term positive. The transforms decrease to a bounded theta-psh s. Plurifine locality on {rho+av>-k}, followed by exhaustion of the finite locus, proves the density inequality using bounded products only. The estimate |rho+av|<=(1+aC)(-rho) gives a uniform positive b, including when the prescribed f is zero.

For the exponential equation, comparison correctly gives w<=v_epsilon and v_epsilon'<=v_epsilon when epsilon'<epsilon. The limit is bounded between w and v_1 and is theta-psh by distributional convergence. The binomial expansion in fixed Omega=theta+omega is exact; mixed bounded monotone continuity handles each term despite its signed smooth coefficient. Dominated convergence handles the equation densities. Bounded exponential domination gives uniqueness even where f vanishes. The lower bound is uniform from b; the upper bound comes from the fixed-Omega Gauduchon mean estimate. Its weighted root integral is comparable to integral f^(1/n)dV, while Holder controls its numerator. Smooth approximation preserves both quantitative density bounds.

For normalized approximants, one fixed Gauduchon metric gives c_j^(1/n)A<=T, with A the fixed weighted root integral and T bounded using theta+omega. No estimate uniform over degenerating Hermitian metrics is assumed. Strict domination after arbitrary translation correctly proves c_j>=b and c_k<=c_j for k>j. Thus c_j decreases to c>0. Uniform exponential integrability in fixed Omega allows gamma q p/(p-q) to be chosen below its integrability exponent, giving a uniform Lq bound for g_j=e^(-gamma phi_j)f. Its root integral remains bounded below because g_j>=f. The already proved exponential theorem supplies bounded w_j, and the shift by -gamma^(-1)log C_0 has the correct sign to give a common lower bound for phi_j.

After subsequence extraction, the upper tail envelopes are in the correct backgrounds and decrease to the canonical L1 limit. Ordered contact gives the stated maximum inequality, including ties. Finite maxima, bounded increasing continuity, and then decreasing continuity with the fixed-background expansion yield MA_theta(phi)>=cf dV.

Every finite lower rooftop has a constant competitor and a continuous obstacle, so accepted contact support applies. On each disjoint contact piece, both potentials are omega_l-psh and ordered contact gives the required upper measure bound. The weight e^(p_(j,N)-h_j) is at least one on that piece; off the contact set the left measure vanishes. Thus the global weighted inequality is valid without a factor counting the obstacles. The decreasing finite rooftops equal P_theta(h_j) in the limit by the two competitor inequalities. Their common bounded range permits dominated convergence of the weighted densities. The lower tail envelopes increase to phi'<=phi, using almost-everywhere convergence and canonical representatives. Their limiting inequality is MA_theta(phi')<=e^(phi'-phi)cf dV<=e^(phi'-phi)MA_theta(phi). Exponential comparison gives phi'>=phi, so equality follows. No Monge-Ampere continuity under arbitrary L1 convergence is assumed.

Normalization preserves the equation and the uniform oscillation bound. Strict domination after translation proves uniqueness of the positive scalar without asserting uniqueness of normalized potentials. The two final exponential barriers give exactly ||lambda v_lambda-log c||_infinity<=lambda osc(phi), and scalar uniqueness implies independence of the auxiliary approximation metric.

All dimension-one steps remain valid: the Gauduchon trace becomes Stokes, the root integral becomes integral f, and the Holder exponent p/(p-1) is finite. The hypotheses are used where needed. Uniformity concerns fixed geometric data and the two stipulated density bounds, with fixed lambda for exponential solutions. Neither existence proof imports BMP, PVP, or a mass bound for all bounded potentials.

The required theorem searches returned unrelated results; subsequent primary-source checking verified Lemma 3.3, Theorem 3.4, and Definition 1.6 in [GL23, arXiv v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2107.01938.pdf). The source requires analytic rho and its unshifted -1/t has the stated range error. The manuscript corrects that error and independently reconstructs the extension to genuine rho; it does not invoke the GL existence theorem as proof. The manuscript and original Rethlas files were left unchanged.
